request: Fix the issues found in stability/stress testing so the user experience is smooth, light and fast
changes: Incrementally merge newly committed captures into deterministic receipt-date/UUID order with one live-list publication, preserving canonical objects and unchanged trash
Defer hidden day/week export grouping and text formatting until the user invokes the action; share eligibility predicates with lightweight menu availability checks
Publish tooltip bounds only for hovered, focused or explicitly visible controls
Use action-only AppState references in capture-copy and content-trail controls while retaining capture-specific observation

Use a native viewport-scoped Explorer list with stable identities and a bounded visible-row anchor during incoming captures; deliberate input, selection, filter, project and size changes release the anchor
Explicitly focus clicked Explorer cards so real Up/Down and Return events reach their scoped handlers, including recycled rows
Recreate only the native List subtree for deliberate type/date regrouping while restoring the selected capture

fixture.coverage: Durable automatic receipts through CaptureStore and AppState.didAutoCapture in the production native host, with synthetic previews and an isolated archive
fixture.limits: The Explorer soak does not exercise the macOS clipboard polling source and does not reproduce the previously sampled hang. Main-queue probe delay is not an animation frame-rate measurement.

harnessRevision.change: Reacquire the currently attached native scroll view before each existing burst/postload scroll and assert its window identity, because deliberate regrouping now replaces the table
harnessRevision.unchanged: Capture count/mix, grouping/resize/scroll/transition sequences, controlled sleeps, minimum exercise time, responsiveness limits and measurement methodology

nativeWarning.text: Application performed a reentrant operation in its NSTableView delegate
nativeWarning.observedPath: Stress settle/layoutSubtreeIfNeeded -> SwiftUI NSHostingView/OutlineListCoordinator.diffRows -> NSTableView endUpdates/top-row stabilization -> NSTableRowHeightData recursive height/total-span cache calculation
nativeWarning.diagnosticMethod: A test-only logging interposer captured the first actual warning and exited 86 intentionally; it is not included in production sources, the project or app
nativeWarning.limitations: The warning is not claimed eliminated. This forced-layout stack does not prove it cannot occur during normal AppKit layout. No crash, hang or failed performance limit occurred in the final uninstrumented stress run.

installedPreviousVersionDiagnosis.finding: Main thread occupied by SwiftUI lazy-stack geometry/layout transactions; normal quit timed out, then the exact verified app PID received SIGTERM

sourceInventory.scope: Offline Python tests, packaging scripts, version plist and metadata; not the complete Swift production inventory

offlineChecks.safety: Temporary fixtures and mocked signing/notary/installer operations only; no network, native build, installation, UI, clipboard or personal archive access

liveChecks: Actual Explorer scroll bar advances during a scroll action
Expand reveals the inspector; Restore returns to compact layout
Auto Capture remains paused; tooltips remain enabled
installation.liveCloseLimit: Hide was invoked, but accessibility retained the window tree; live hidden-state completion is not claimed. Native close/reopen behavior passes the isolated full suite and stress tests.

limitations: Passing isolated tests cannot guarantee that the application will never freeze
The remaining native row-height diagnostic is documented, not suppressed or claimed fixed
Large-payload/OCR pressure, hours-long operation and macOS 14 runtime are not covered by the synthetic stress result
Local tests and source packaging checks do not establish Apple signing, distribution readiness or App Store approval
